chapter.p: LEChapter23 Verse1 The decree about Babylon, that Isaiah the son of Amoz was shown. VerseEnd
chapter.li: Verse2 Lift up a banner on the high mountain, shout to them, beckon them to enter the royal gates. VerseEnd Verse3 I’ve commanded the ones I’ve prepared for battle, and assembled warriors to execute My judgment, those who rejoice in My triumph. VerseEnd Verse4 Listen to the noise on the mountains, like a great multitude preparing and massing together, for the Lord Almighty is marshaling an army for war. VerseEnd Verse5 They come from distant lands, from the end of heaven — the Lord and the weapons of His wrath — to destroy the whole country. VerseEnd

Verse6 Start wailing, for the day of the Lord is coming; it will come like destruction from the Almighty. VerseEnd Verse7 Everyone will faint, everyone’s heart will sink, VerseEnd Verse8 and they’ll be overcome by terror. Pain and fear will seize them, they’ll thrash about like a woman in childbirth, looking in horror at each other’s shocked faces. VerseEnd Verse9 See, the day of the Lord is coming, cruel, wrathful, and full of fierce anger, to make the land desolate and destroy the sinners occupying it. VerseEnd Verse10 For the stars above and the constellations won’t be seen; the rising sun will be darkened, and the moon won’t permit her light to shine. VerseEnd Verse11 I’ll punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. I’ll put an end to the arrogance of the proud and knock down the cruelty of the ruthless. VerseEnd Verse12 Survivors will be more refined than pure gold, and it will be harder to find people than the gold of Ophir. VerseEnd Verse13 Therefore I’ll shake the heavens, and the earth will violently quake in response to the anger of the Lord of Hosts on that day. VerseEnd Verse14 Then like chased deer or wild sheep, everyone will try to gather with friends and flee to a safe place. VerseEnd Verse15 Whoever is captured will be torn apart, men will be slaughtered. VerseEnd Verse16 Their infants will be dashed to pieces while they watch, their houses will be robbed, and their wives abused. VerseEnd Verse17 I’ll bring the Medes against them, who don’t value silver and gold. VerseEnd Verse18 Their weapons will massacre the young men, and they’ll have no pity for infants; they won’t spare the children. VerseEnd

Verse19 Then Babylon, jewel of kingdoms, the pride and joy of the Babylonians, will be destroyed by God like Sodom and Gomorrah. VerseEnd Verse20 She’ll never be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation, nomads won’t pitch a tent there, and shepherds won’t rest their flocks there. VerseEnd Verse21 Instead, wild desert animals will occupy it, jackals will enter their abandoned houses, and owls will live there, and wild goats will leap about. VerseEnd Verse22 Hyenas and jackals will roam within her abandoned walls. Her time is close at hand, and her days won’t continue. I’ll destroy her speedily. Indeed, I’ll be merciful to My people, but the wicked will perish. VerseEnd

LEChapter24 Verse1 The Lord will have compassion for Jacob, and will again choose Israel, and bring them back to their own land. Foreigners will join and be included with the house of Jacob. VerseEnd Verse2 Nations will bring them back to their homeland from the ends of the earth, and they’ll return to their lands of promise. The house of Israel will allow them to become the Lord’s servants and handmaids; and Israel will be captors instead of captives, masters without taskmasters. VerseEnd Verse3 On that day the Lord will give 2PSI you rest from 2PSI your sorrow and trouble, from the hard times 2PSI you had to endure, VerseEnd

Verse4 2PSI You’ll tell this proverb to the king of Babylon, saying: How has the taskmaster vanished, and how has the oppression ended? VerseEnd Verse5 The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the king, VerseEnd Verse6 used to abuse people in wrath with continual beatings, and in fury conquered nations with his aggression; he’s now persecuted, and no one is stopping it. VerseEnd Verse7 The whole earth is at rest and peaceful; they begin singing. VerseEnd Verse8 Even the junipers and the cedars of Lebanon gloat over 2PSI your fall, saying: Now that 2PSI you’ve been dropped to the ground no one will come to cut us down! VerseEnd Verse9 The dead in hell are looking forward to 2PSI your arrival. The departed anticipate greeting 2PSI you. Former leaders and kings are rising from their thrones in anticipation of 2PSI you joining them in hell. VerseEnd Verse10 They’ll all say to 2PSI you: 2PSI You’re as weak now as we are; 2PSI you’re now one of us. VerseEnd Verse11 All 2PSI your magnificence fell into the grave, along with the noise of 2PSI your harps; maggots and worms are now covering 2PSI you. VerseEnd

Verse12 How have 2PSI you fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! 2PSI You’ve been cast down to the earth, 2PSI you who once destroyed whole nations! VerseEnd Verse13 2PSI You said in 2PSI your heart: I’ll ascend into heaven; I’ll sit on a throne above the stars of God; I’ll be enthroned on the mount of the congregation, in the northern sky; VerseEnd Verse14 I’ll ascend above the highest clouds; I’ll make myself like the Most High! VerseEnd Verse15 But 2PSI you’ve been brought down to hell, to the deepest pit. VerseEnd Verse16 Those who notice 2PSI you stare at 2PSI you, pondering 2PSI your fate. They ask: Is this the man who shook the earth, who controlled kingdoms, VerseEnd Verse17 and turned the world into a wilderness, and overthrew its cities and didn’t let his prisoners return home? VerseEnd

Verse18 All the kings of the nations lie in state, each buried in their own tomb. VerseEnd Verse19 But 2PSI you’ve been left on the ground like a rejected branch; 2PSI your unburied carcass now rotting on the ground, stabbed through by a sword. VerseEnd Verse20 2PSI You weren’t mourned or buried because 2PSI you destroyed 2PSI your land and killed 2PSI your people. Let the children of 2PSI your wicked people never remember 2PSI your name. VerseEnd Verse21 Prepare a place to slaughter 2PSI your children for the sins 2PSI you committed, they are never to rise to inherit any land or ever again control a city. VerseEnd Verse22 I’ll prevent it, says the Lord of Hosts, I’ll wipe out Babylon’s name and any of her survivors or descendants, declares the Lord. VerseEnd Verse23 I’ll turn it into an abandoned swampland, and I’ll make its destruction complete, says the Lord of Hosts. VerseEnd

Verse24 The Lord of Hosts has promised, saying: Just as I’ve planned, it will happen; and My purposes will control events. VerseEnd Verse25 I’ll defeat the Assyrian in My land, and on My mountains trample him down. Then his chains will be removed from My people, and his burdens taken off their shoulders. VerseEnd Verse26 This is My plan set for the whole earth, and this is My hand stretched out over all nations. VerseEnd Verse27 For the Lord of Hosts has a plan, and who can thwart it? Who’s able to fight against His hand? VerseEnd
chapter.p: Verse28 The year king Ahaz died I received this prophecy from the Lord: VerseEnd
chapter.li: Verse29 2PSI You Philistines shouldn’t rejoice over the club that struck 2PSI you being broken, because from that snake’s root will come a viper, a darting, poisonous serpent. VerseEnd Verse30 And the poorest of the poor will be fed, and the needy will rest safely. And I’ll kill 2PSI your root with famine, killing all 2PSI your survivors. VerseEnd Verse31 Wail at 2PSI your gate; howl in 2PSI your city; melt away all 2PSI you Philistines, for a cloud of smoke is coming from the north against 2PSI you at the appointed time. VerseEnd Verse32 What’s the message to all the nations? That Zion has been established and there His people will find safety. VerseEnd
